plan.title: Sector presets — full-coverage startup-tech database bootstrap
plan.summary: Ship a curated list of tech startup sectors and a --preset flag on sweep:auto so one command progressively builds comprehensive M&A coverage across the entire startup ecosystem. A single `ptbot sweep:auto --preset startup-tech --geography 'United States' --environment <env>` sweeps all ~35 sectors over the configured years, filling gaps as it goes.
plan.motivation: The database gets exponentially more useful as coverage expands across sectors. Today users have to manually enumerate sectors. A preset bakes in the industry knowledge — every major tech vertical is covered — and lets the sweep run unattended, picking up where it left off on each execution. Run it weekly and the database self-maintains.
deliverables: sectors/ directory at project root with curated JSON preset files
sectors/startup-tech.json: ~35 tech startup verticals (FinTech, HealthTech, AI/ML, Cybersecurity, SaaS, DevTools, CleanTech, etc.) each with a canonical name and optional aliases
--preset NAME flag on ptbot sweep:auto that loads sectors from sectors/{name}.json instead of --sectors CSV. Mutually exclusive with --sectors.
ptbot db:coverage command: prints a coverage table showing which sector×year combinations exist in the DB vs. are missing. Helps operators see what the next sweep will fill in.
startup-sectors.toml: ready-to-use ptbot-sweep TOML config referencing all startup-tech sectors for users who prefer the TOML runner
Tests covering: preset loading, unknown preset error, coverage command with seeded DB, sweep:auto --preset dry-run
README section: ## Building full-sector coverage with examples
constraints: Preset files are plain JSON — no external data sources required
sectors/ ships with the package so presets work after pip install
Frozen models — do not change DealCandidate or ResearchParams
--preset and --sectors are mutually exclusive; both missing is an error
ptbot db:coverage must work gracefully when the DB does not exist yet
